newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan investors stay on sidelines in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan investors stay on sidelines in quiet trade.

text.p: Jordan's bourse was quiet on Monday in minimal trade with most investors in a wait-and-see mood over political developments, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell 0.02 percent to 152.32 points in poor turnover worth 200,349 dinars ($282,978).

The market, traditionally sensitive to political twists and turns in the Middle East peace process, has also been hit by a tight monetary policy which investors blame for a constant liquidity shortage.
Dealers say lack of institutional trade was further weakening trade in depressed activity overshadowed by the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan, when buyers are scarce.
Delays in agreeing this year's trade protocol between Amman and Baghdad also weighed heavily on the market, which surged last month on Iraq's U.N.-approved oil-for-food deal.
Trucking firm Unified Land Transport, expected to benefit from any increase in shipments to Iraq, was again the heaviest traded stock rising 0.04 dinars to 2.14 in trade worth nearly 44,984 dinars.
National Industries, a firm manufacturing sanitary paper which has been performing well on healthy export orders, was the top gainer in the lacklustre market, rising 2.94 percent to 0.70 dinars.
Gaining shares outnumbered losers by 13 to seven, while shares in fifteen others were traded but unchanged.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange fell 0.06 percent to 82.03 points from 82.07.
